title: Flow Burstiness Calculation
description: Measures the burstiness of network traffic flow to detect sudden packet spikes typical in DoS attacks.
features: total_pkts, dur_safe
detection: Calculated strictly as total_pkts / dur_safe. Prevents double division errors.
mitigation: Used internally by the models for rapid anomaly detection.

title: Real-time Flow Tracking Context
description: Defines how individual network flows are tracked and identified in real-time.
features: initiator_ip
detection: Flows are mapped and behavioral context is retrieved using the initiator_ip rather than generic canonical keys.
mitigation: Ensures accurate attribution of malicious behavior to the correct source.

title: Feature Set Exclusions
description: Guidelines on feature selection for the live IDS detection engine.
features: Packet Size Entropy
detection: The 'Packet Size Entropy' feature is explicitly removed from the live classification pipeline as it cannot be reliably computed in real-time.
mitigation: Ensures dataset integrity and prevents real-time pipeline latency.

title: OSI Model
description: A conceptual framework standardizing the functions of a telecommunication system into seven layers: Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application.
features: Layer 2 (MAC), Layer 3 (IP), Layer 4 (TCP/UDP), Layer 7 (HTTP/DNS).
detection: IDS systems monitor Layers 3 and 4 for flow data, and Layer 7 for payload anomalies.
mitigation: N/A - Conceptual Framework.

title: TCP/IP Protocol Suite
description: The foundational communication protocols for the internet, operating primarily on four layers: Network Access, Internet, Transport, and Application.
features: Connection-oriented (TCP) and connectionless (UDP) transport.
detection: Anomalies in TCP flags (SYN, ACK, FIN, RST) indicate state manipulation attacks.
mitigation: Proper subnetting and strict firewall ACLs.

title: Subnetting and CIDR
description: The practice of dividing a network into two or more smaller networks. Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) is a method for allocating IP addresses and IP routing.
features: Subnet masks, IP ranges, Broadcast IDs, Network IDs.
detection: Detecting attacks trying to scan across different subnet boundaries.
mitigation: VLAN segregation and strict routing policies to isolate critical systems.

title: VLAN (Virtual Local Area Network)
description: Any broadcast domain that is partitioned and isolated in a computer network at the data link layer (OSI layer 2).
features: 802.1Q tagging, broadcast isolation.
detection: Monitoring for VLAN hopping attacks (Double Tagging).
mitigation: Disable Dynamic Trunking Protocol (DTP), put unused ports in a dead VLAN.

title: NAT (Network Address Translation)
description: A method of mapping an IP address space into another by modifying network address information in the IP header of packets while they are in transit.
features: Public vs Private IPs, Port Address Translation (PAT).
detection: Correlating internal IP addresses with external translated IPs during incident response.
mitigation: Hides internal network structure from external reconnaissance.

title: Transmission Control Protocol (TCP)
description: A connection-oriented communications protocol that facilitates the exchange of messages between computing devices in a network.
features: Three-way handshake (SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK), reliable delivery, sequencing.
detection: High rate of incomplete handshakes indicates network scanning or DoS.
mitigation: TCP timeout tuning, stateful packet inspection.

title: User Datagram Protocol (UDP)
description: A communications protocol that is primarily used to establish low-latency and loss-tolerating connections between applications on the internet.
features: Connectionless, no handshakes, fast transmission, susceptible to spoofing.
detection: Sudden massive spikes in UDP traffic on random ports.
mitigation: Rate limiting UDP traffic on edge routers.

title: SYN Flood Attack
description: A DoS attack targeting the TCP handshake by sending a massive succession of SYN requests to exhaust connection queues.
features: High SYN packet rate, extremely low ACK completion ratio, massive half-open connections.
detection: Observed severe SYN >> ACK imbalance from an initiator_ip.
mitigation: SYN cookies deployment, TCP timeout tuning, automated firewall filtering.

title: UDP Flood Attack
description: A volumetric DoS attack where the attacker overwhelms random ports on the targeted host with IP packets containing UDP datagrams.
features: Exceptionally high rate of UDP packets, random destination ports.
detection: High 'total_pkts' over a short 'dur_safe' specifically over UDP protocol.
mitigation: Rate limiting UDP traffic, utilizing upstream scrubbing centers.

title: Port Scan Reconnaissance
description: Attackers probe server ports to map open services and find vulnerabilities.
features: High destination port diversity from a single initiator_ip, frequent TCP RST responses.
detection: Rapid connection attempts to multiple distinct ports over a short time.
mitigation: Stateful firewalls configured to block IP addresses exhibiting sweep behavior.

title: Brute Force Attack
description: A trial-and-error method to decode encrypted data or passwords through exhaustive effort.
features: High volume of login requests, identical payload sizes indicating failed attempts.
detection: Tracking repetitive failed authentication attempts originating from a specific initiator_ip.
mitigation: Account lockout policies, Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA), fail2ban.

title: SQL Injection (SQLi)
description: Interfering with queries an application makes to its database.
features: Presence of SQL meta-characters (', --, #) in payloads.
detection: Layer 7 DPI looking for anomalous string patterns like 'OR 1=1' in HTTP GET/POST.
mitigation: Prepared Statements (Parameterized Queries), strict input validation, WAF.

title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
description: Injection attacks wherein malicious scripts are injected into otherwise benign and trusted websites.
features: Payloads containing <script> tags or JavaScript event handlers in URLs or inputs.
detection: WAF rules analyzing HTTP request parameters for script signatures.
mitigation: Context-aware output encoding, Content Security Policy (CSP).

title: Man in the Middle (MitM)
description: An attacker secretly relays and possibly alters the communications between two parties who believe they are directly communicating.
features: Unexpected MAC address changes (ARP Spoofing), SSL certificate mismatches.
detection: ARP cache monitoring, detecting downgraded encryption protocols.
mitigation: Dynamic ARP Inspection (DAI), enforcing HTTPS/HSTS, VPNs.

title: CIA Triad
description: Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability - the core model for info security policies.
features: Confidentiality (encryption), Integrity (hashing), Availability (redundancy).
detection: Breaches impact these pillars. DoS impacts Availability. MitM impacts Confidentiality.
mitigation: Cryptography, continuous monitoring, highly available architectures.

title: Authentication vs Authorization
description: Authentication verifies WHO you are (identity). Authorization verifies WHAT you can do (permissions).
features: AuthN uses passwords/MFA. AuthZ uses RBAC/ABAC.
detection: Privilege Escalation attacks bypass AuthZ. Brute Force bypasses AuthN.
mitigation: Implement MFA for AuthN, and Principle of Least Privilege for AuthZ.

title: Signature vs Anomaly Detection
description: Signature detection looks for known bad patterns (like antivirus). Anomaly detection creates a baseline of normal traffic and flags deviations.
features: Signatures are fast but miss zero-days. Anomaly uses ML/Stats but has higher false positives.
detection: Modern Hybrid IDS (like AI Wireshark) uses both methodologies concurrently.
mitigation: Continuous updates for signatures, continuous model retraining for anomalies.
references: NIST SP 800-94 (Guide to Intrusion Detection and Prevention Systems)

title: Random Forest Algorithm
description: An ensemble learning method for classification that operates by constructing a multitude of decision trees and outputting the mode of the classes.
features: Robust against overfitting, provides feature importance.
detection: Used as a primary classifier to differentiate benign traffic from attacks using network flow features.
mitigation: Hyperparameter tuning (e.g., n_estimators, max_depth) prevents model drift.

title: CIC-IDS2017 Dataset
description: A comprehensive cybersecurity dataset containing benign and common attacks, closely resembling true real-world data (PCAPs and flow features).
features: Includes Brute Force, DoS, Web Attacks, Infiltration, Botnet, and DDoS.
detection: Serves as the benchmark for training and testing ML models in network intrusion detection.
mitigation: N/A - Used for model training and evaluation.

title: Spydera (INMIDS) Core Concept
description: Spydera, technically known as INMIDS (Intelligent Network Monitoring & Intrusion Detection System), is an advanced desktop-based cybersecurity platform acting as an 'AI Wireshark'. It merges real-time network visibility (packet capture) with AI-driven threat intelligence in a single unified interface.
features: PyQt5 Frameless GUI, Flask REST API, SQLite WAL Database, C++ fast_sniffer.
detection: Utilizes a multi-stage pipeline: packet capture, flow normalization, hybrid AI threat analysis, and automated C2 response.
mitigation: Solves tool fragmentation and high latency by providing zero-latency automated processing without requiring multiple software tools like Wireshark and Snort.

title: Spydera Technology Stack & Architecture
description: Spydera is built on a 5-layer hybrid architecture. It uses C++ (fast_sniffer) for high-speed packet capture, Python/Scapy for flow processing, Flask for the REST API (C2 Backend), and React/PyQt5 for the presentation layer.
features: C++ libpcap engine (up to 800k pkt/s), Producer-Consumer threading, SQLite WAL mode, Flask API on port 5000.
detection: Captures raw Ethernet frames using Npcap/C++, passes them via shared-memory ring buffer to Python, converts them to 18-field flow dictionaries, and feeds them to the AI Engine.
mitigation: The hybrid stack ensures wire-speed capture without sacrificing the flexibility of Python's ML ecosystem.

title: Spydera AI Detection Engine (5 Families)
description: The AI Core Engine in Spydera operates in real-time, executing six sequential detection stages to identify both known and zero-day threats.
features: Flood Detection, TCP Anomaly, ARP Spoofing (MITM), DNS Tunneling, Deep Payload Inspection (DPI).
detection: Analyzes PPS/Bandwidth for Floods, flag anomalies (XMAS/NULL/SYN) for TCP, MAC-IP bindings for ARP, query volume/entropy for DNS, and applies 8 regex signatures (SQLi, XSS, RCE, LFI) on payloads up to 4096 bytes.
mitigation: Generates severity-coded alerts (1 to 5). Features a 10-second alert cooldown per IP to prevent UI/Database flooding during sustained attacks.

title: Spydera Ransomware Behavior Analyzer
description: A specialized sub-component of Spydera's AI that targets advanced persistent threats (APTs) and ransomware through cumulative multi-signal behavioral scoring.
features: C2 Beaconing (CV < 0.15), DGA Domain Entropy (> 4.2), SMB Lateral Movement, Large Internal Data Transfers.
detection: Aggregates weak signals over time. If the combined weight of evidence crosses a threshold (100 points), it flags a RANSOMWARE_CRITICAL alert.
mitigation: Automatically triggers the DEFCON 1 protocol upon reaching severity 5.

title: Spydera Machine Learning Layers (Random Forest & Isolation Forest)
description: Spydera uses two ML models trained on the CICIDS2017 dataset to classify flows with high precision and detect zero-day anomalies.
features: Random Forest (Supervised, 31 features, 200 estimators) and Isolation Forest (Unsupervised, Baseline anomaly detection).
detection: Random Forest handles known families (DoS, PortScan, Brute Force) with near 100% accuracy. Isolation Forest establishes a benign baseline and flags statistically distant volumetric flows (zero-days) that bypass signatures.
mitigation: Features undergo Variance Threshold, Correlation Filtering, and Log Transformation to ensure high-speed real-time classification.

title: Spydera DEFCON 1 Auto-Containment Protocol
description: Spydera's automated incident response mechanism for critical threats (Severity 5).
features: Windows Firewall isolation, process freezing, C2 channel preservation.
detection: Triggered automatically by events like Gateway ARP Spoofing or Ransomware Critical scores.
mitigation: Isolates the affected endpoint at the Windows Firewall level, terminating malicious processes while keeping the secure C2 TLS connection alive for forensic investigation by SOC analysts.

title: Spydera Remote Agents and C2 Architecture
description: Spydera is not just a local tool; it supports a distributed enterprise architecture where lightweight remote agents feed traffic to a centralized Command and Control (C2) server.
features: Dynamic Discovery (GitHub Gist, DuckDNS, LAN UDP), Fernet Payload Encryption, JWT Authentication.
detection: Agents capture local traffic on endpoints and send structured flow dicts to the central Flask API. Enables cross-agent correlation to detect lateral movement across subnets.
mitigation: Commands and data are serialized to JSON, compressed via zlib, encrypted with AES-128-CBC (Fernet), and Base64 encoded for stealthy, secure transmission.
